utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is the Case Number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radislav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you following the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I can follow, and I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Anna Richterova for the Prosecution assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you. Appearances for Radislav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. David Cunningham with Barbara Baruch. We are assisted today by Vesna Anic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, too. Are there any preliminaries before we bring in the witness? Yes, Madam Baruch.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe Mr. Ackerman has filed a motion with regard to the next witness. We received --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The one we're hearing this morning? No, next week.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: We received 55 pages in B/C/S that were labelled by the Prosecutor, not by us, as Rule 68 information, which is essential to have for the preparation of cross-examination. I've spoken with Ms. Richterova. We are trying to work out a way that I would have it at least the night before I did cross-examination, and at this point, as you know, we are working without a case manager who speaks B/C/S, and so it's very difficult. And I'm not quite as advanced as this Tribunal in understanding B/C/S at this moment, although I try to learn a little every day. And so we have made a motion to postpone the witness, but as I've told you, we are working with Ms. Richterova. It's actually Ms. Korner's witness. She will be taking him on direct, so perhaps by the end of the day I will have more to say. But at this point, I do not have a translation of this Rule 68 information, and Ms. Richterova informs me that the Prosecutor probably doesn't have an English translation because it would be my understanding that if the Prosecutor was in possession of an English translation, it would be appropriate to turn that over as part of it being Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which witness are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 7.113. And you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does he enjoy protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We are checking. I think he is not, but I'm sorry I do not have my list with me. I will have a look at this material --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have a look now if you can because the name has been mentioned, and if necessary, we will have to redact it --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No protective measures. All right. So always be careful, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I would have been more careful, except I know a little bit about this witness, and I strongly suspect that he wouldn't be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we will have more as we go along, and have an update on the information. Ms. Korner is already aware of the situation?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will have a look at the materials first, and I only want to say that we disclosed them on the 14th of May, and we never translate Rule 68 materials. Anyway, but I will do my best, and I will inform also Ms. Korner about the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The reason why I'm standing is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to look taller.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: She doesn't have to with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's about the way how to present the material of Mr. Kaiser. As you are aware, we disclosed, and we also handed over CDs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: With the annexes, with pictures. And we would like to tender into exhibit the CD, not the hard copies. I have one hard copy with me. I spoke with the Defence, and I told him that this one hard copy which is on my desk is identical to the CD. And during the presentation, I would refer to pictures which I have here, but at the end of the day, I would like to tender the CD. And now, it's up to you or up to the registry to tell the Prosecution whether we can tender the CD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Prosecution or -- first of all, I need a feedback from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I have no reason to doubt what's on the CD is the same thing that's in the hard copy. I would have no objection to this procedure based on the representations of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. The next thing -- thank you, Mr. Cunningham. The next thing I want to say about this is that in the list of exhibits which will be potentially used by Dr. Colin Kaiser, there is, first line precisely, this CD. And then in the second line, there is another CD, CD with documents 0179-8778/9340, which I don't have. I have a CD here, which has been given to me, but this refers to the first of these two CDs, in other words starting with Document 5207 and finishing with Document or page 5590.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So please tell me what --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: That I believe the other CD was given to you, but we have an extract of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When was it given to us?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we do not have the date. But it was given to you with Rule 92 bis witness statements because this other CD refers to the Witness 7.243. On these CDs are books of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I'm not saying that we haven't, but I need to check this. Madam Registrar, could you please contact my secretary and ask her to locate amongst the Rule 92 bis documents a CD with the following reference number: 0179- -- you have the -- okay -- and to come back to you or to me ASAP. All right. So it's agreed and it's our decision that the documents that you intend to tender in exhibit will be so tendered in the CD-ROM format.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to give this a number and explain that it contains pages or reference -- what number are we going to give to this CD?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's P1881.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P1881. And I need someone to check here and now that it is not a defective CD. And that it contains nothing more than what is indicated, that is 0323-5207 to 0323-5590, with the understanding, Mrs. Baruch, and Mr. Cunningham, that you can verify the contents of this CD at your leisure and pleasure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. That's fine with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, it's P1881.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, in the meantime, I'm checking the CD myself. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The witness is waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, usher, could you bring the witness in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Kaiser, Dr. Kaiser.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome to this Tribunal. Could you please check the audiosystem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put it on number 4, please. Put it on number 4. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hear you in English, and I had you in French before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. Well, I'm bilingual.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Myself as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome to this Tribunal. You're about to give evidence related to your expert report. It's the practice of this Tribunal that before you give testimony, you make a solemn declaration equivalent to an oath, the text of which is contained in a document -- in a piece of paper that the usher is going to hand to you. Please stand up and read that aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you start giving evidence, I should like to draw your attention to something which is very important and which would make the life of each and every one of us here a little bit lighter, easier. And that is you are English speaking, I'm English speaking, Madam Richterova is English speaking, the Defence team is English speaking. It's only the accused who is not English speaking, and by our statute, we need to interpret every word that you say also in French, apart from the Serbo-Croat. Being all English speaking, we usually fall into a common trap, and that is not giving a -- allowing a short interval of time between question and answer, and that spells trouble and difficulties for the interpreters. So I ask of you and Madam Richterova and later on Mr. Cunningham or Madam Baruch to adhere to this rule, allow a short interval of time between question and answer, and please speak slowly, at a slow pace, because otherwise we will have problems. All right? Thanks. Madam Richterova will be conducting the examination-in-chief. And she will be followed next by the Defence on cross-examination. Thank you. Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you be to kind and state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: My name is Colin Reid Erlin Kaiser.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I think one of the microphones doesn't work. Now it's okay. Dr. Kaiser, is it correct that you have testified in this Tribunal in front of this Tribunal already on two occasions?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you remember in which cases and approximately the date?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: First, in 1996 for count 61 or 66 against General Mladic and Radovan Karadzic. And second time in 1998 in the case against General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for your information, Madam Baruch and Mr. Cunningham, assuming that you're perhaps not that familiar with this particular procedure, because proceedings, the trial against Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Mladic, as such, hasn't really started, but there is Rule 61 on the basis of which testimonies -- evidence of certain witnesses can be heard and should be heard. And the testimony of Dr. Kaiser was heard precisely in terms of Rule 61. Okay, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Is it correct that in these two trials, or in these two testimonies, you gave a general overview on damage destruction of sacral buildings in Bosnia-Herzegovina, about your involvement in the study of sacral and culture monuments in the former Yugoslavia? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: In 1996, it was specifically targeted on cultural heritage in general, and of course included sacral buildings which could be considered cultural heritage. In 1998, it was more specifically about sacral buildings, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Just to speed up your testimony today, I would like to tender into evidence these two transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any objection on the part of the Defence, Madam Baruch?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, it is my understanding that these transcripts are being offered by the Prosecution because in the prior testimony, the witness went over his definitions of religious buildings and some other terminology that would assist the Court. To the extent that testimony is contained in those transcripts, we don't have any objection to it because I think that would save a lot of redundancy before the Tribunal today. So the extent that they go beyond that and it contains matters that are not relevant to this proceeding, of course we would object. But knowing as Your Honour has told me many times being a professional judge, you'll be able to separate that out. I just wanted that objection on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to tender the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what do you have to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I agree. Of course, what goes beyond the matter subject of today's testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay. So it's our decision that, decision of the Trial Chamber, that this transcript -- these transcripts are so admitted into evidence with the caveat that has been explained by Mr. Cunningham and agreed to by the Prosecution. We need to give them a number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The transcript from the year 1996 will be P1882.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the Karadzic and the Mladic, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. And the transcript from the year 1998 will be P1882.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dr. Kaiser, I would like to ask you now if you can give us just very brief information about your professional and educational --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we need that. He has given that already in the Karadzic transcript starting from page 2. I think we can be practical, and you just ask him question when he was asked the same question in the other proceedings, his answer was correct or not, and if he does confirm that it was correct, we can move ahead and take it as it is on the face of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I only asked you because you testified last time in 1998, did anything change in respect to your profession?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you more qualified, more experienced? Do you think there's anything else we ought to know regarding your academic background and credentials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think for the professional background, there's perhaps two things that are worth knowing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm a UNESCO functionary, that's something to be kept in mind, my cooperation with the Tribunal, it's a cooperation of UNESCO, with ICTY. In 1999 in July, I was sent to Kosovo in order to look at the situation, get a general idea of the situation of cultural sacral buildings there, and it was a brief mission. And I would just like to point out that I rang the bell very strongly inasmuch as the imminent dangers facing the Serbian Orthodox heritage was concerned. I think that's worth keeping in mind. In the first half of 2002, I, again as UNESCO functionary, set up a cultural heritage monitoring system with the OSCE, in FYROM, the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, specially functioning in the zones which government officials could not have access to, as I say ethnic Albanian zones. We were concerned particularly about what was happening to Macedonian Orthodox churches. So this is additional information that I think may be of some relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You were asked, Dr. Kaiser, to produce a report on the damaging and destruction of Islamic and Roman Catholic sacral buildings. You focus on six municipalities, Bosanski Novi, Donji Vakuf, Kljuc, Kotor Varos, Prijedor and Sanski Most. My first question, was it your selection, or were you tasked to focus on these six municipalities?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: As I best remember, I was tasked to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After you arrived to The Hague, you were given some additional materials, and you produced supplement to the report on the damaging and destruction of Islamic and Roman Catholic sacral buildings. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will go into details how you prepare this supplement, but at this stage, I would like to tender into evidence the report and the supplement to the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I want to make sure that we're talking about the same documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We're supposedly talking of a document which has pages 10033 -- sorry, if I start with the ERN number, it's 01150372. And finishes at 01150565. This is called -- it was a title "Military Developments in the Bosanska Krajina" -- sorry, sorry, sorry. Sorry. I'm mixing one document with the other. It starts with 01147393 and finishes - correct me if I am wrong Madam Richterova - 01147408. That's...

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other one forget, because it's something I have in the file here which I brought with me but which has got nothing to do with this witness. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, with respect to that document which is his report on the damage and destruction, we have a copy of that. We have no objection to that. I don't know if the Prosecution wishes to offer the supplement that he provided that he has since done, that was provided to us yesterday that contained -- begins with the number 02932200 through 203 inclusive. We would also have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, we wish to offer this supplement into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And this will be under P1883.1. This is the report. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The supplement will be?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Will be P1883.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that that is agreeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, so we can move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And I think this will be the time to tender into evidence one more document which has something to do with Dr. Kaiser's report, and it is his table which goes together with the photographs. And this table is also on the CD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: But I have a hard copy because it will be easier for all parties to go through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: -- The hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the purposes of this sitting, we better work on the basis of the hard copies because for me, for example, to refer to the CD, I have to forget the transcript and have the CD content superimposed on the transcript, and I won't be able to follow the two things at the same time. So if you have hard copies --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I had only small problem, and after we finish these problems, hopefully we will already go smoothly. It's because this table is on the CD, do you want to assign separate exhibit number for this document or shall we use the exhibit which was already assigned to the CD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, we will use the same number that has been assigned to it on the CD.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because that's the only way it makes sense. On the other hand for the purpose of the sitting as such, we will refer to the hard copies, because it will make everybody's life easier. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we won't have two documents identical and bearing two different exhibit numbers because it wouldn't make sense. All right. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dr. Kaiser, when you were tasked to evaluate the damage on sacral buildings in these six municipalities, were you given any materials based on which information did you proceed in your evaluation and in your work?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: I was given a certain number of materials by ICTY. I was given a series of summary statements of witnesses who had information pertaining to the damaging or destruction of mosques or churches. I was given some information which emanated from the Islamic communities as well, the medzlis. I was given some photographs which are reproduced, in fact, are on the CD, which were taken by the teams of ICTY. I think those are the main sorts of documents that, in fact, I were given. And a certain number of reference books in fact I didn't have in my possession as well, notably the book of Muharem Omerdic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show you some documents, and I would like you to confirm whether you used them or not. These documents are marked like attachments to the statement of the witness 7.243. The reason why I want to show these documents to this witness is that the Defence objected to using these attachments with the Rule 92 bis statement of Witness 7.243. I would first start with showing these documents to the witness. This is a document from Prijedor, and it is attachment 1. And just, please, have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the top of this document, I believe that you have these attachments in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: On the top of this document is a document in B/C/S. I was a translation of these documents, and I will provide you with this translation right away, and I will ask the usher to place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Okay, the document on Prijedor, yes, I've used this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can the witness explain what's the Medzlis Islamska zajednice essentially is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Islamic community board for the municipality, basically. The organisation of the community is according to the municipality, does not seem to be according to a hierarchy as it would be in the Catholic church or the Orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you use this document during your work?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: I used this document, yes. I used it because it's a good document. It's also a document which although there's some attachment, it says it was handed in year 2000, it contains information I think that was compiled before then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How did you utilise this document?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: This document has -- the first part of it is sort of a list of Islamic community properties, sacral buildings. Mektebs, I think Gasulhanas and things like that in it. It's a useful document because it indicated some buildings that I couldn't find, for example, in Muharem Omerdic's book on the chapter that was on Prijedor. Document is useful because it has photographs that were taken just after the war. It's very important, that is to say, they were taken before a lot of the buildings were pulled down and repaired. It contains some information on damaging. The perspective of the document is really clearly in terms of reconstruction, therefore, the notations that occur at the bottom of these types of pages, karton objekta, when I checked these with the buildings, these are pretty accurate, and there's information on damaging as well, dates of damaging. So it's a good document. Not a complete exhaustive document, but a good one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And on the top, as I just provided you with the translation is a certificate from Prijedor Islamic community and this certifies that the supply -- that we have supplied reliable data for the building, record cards of mosques in the area covered by our medzlis. So this is one document which you used.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, now I'm again facing a small problem because I would like to tender this document into evidence. And as I said, these documents were previously submitted by Witness 7.243, which we would like to tender into evidence in accordance with Rule 92 bis. And the Defence objected. I can tender this document into evidence under this witness, or we can discuss tendering of this evidence when we are discussing Rule 92 bis witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I need to know, because when we start talking and referring to numbers, witnesses in particular, you always catch me on the wrong foot because I can't possibly, humanly speaking, remember each and every one of them by number and whether we have handed down a decision pertaining to the Rule 92 bis applicability or otherwise. Can anyone check for us whether -- as regards Witness 7.243 we have handed down a decision on -- we haven't. So is it still pending? It's still pending. I don't think it's fair to pre-empt that matter by admitting this document now, not through the door but through the window. But it depends. Were you aware of this document, as I would presume that you were, and when was it made available to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was aware of the document because I used the document as the basis for the trips that I carried out. When was it made available? It was made available through ICTY in Sarajevo in maybe 2001. 2001, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You state you affirm that you made use of it in the course of your investigations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I made use of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that solves the matter. Is there objection, Mr. Cunningham, on having this document admitted now in this witness's testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, we don't -- consistent with the objection that Mr. Ackerman filed with the 92 bis, we would renew that objection. Can I have just a moment to confer with Ms. Baruch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was the basis of the objection? Can we check? If we can check on that, we should be able to --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have the motion of the Defence, and it states only that the document is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.text: Okay. First of all, these documents I consider they are in fact three documents. utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I only want to ask because Dr. Kaiser already went through Prijedor and Sanski Most. So you are now referring to these four --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are referring to now P1884.3, which is -- 1884.4, which is Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dr. Kaiser, you heard the Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there anything you think we ought to know about the origin of this document and the contents of this document in a general way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. These are documents that all of them use the same karton objekta. These documents seem to share something in common. I think that their date of establishment is not so ancient. It looks like it has been done fairly recently, in the last few years. The documents are interesting to help to find, say, a mekteb existed or a mesdzid existed somewhere, so this is another one to look for. They are very useful as a list. The information on them is not -- there's some dates, but, for example, Kotor Varos, nearly everything is dated damaging is done the month of July. I find this a little bit -- it raises questions. All of a sudden, somebody says this happened in July, you didn't make an effort to find out anything else. Some of them don't have very much in the way of damaging information. There are other documents, I believe, attached to these. For example, we have Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now you are talking about Kljuc, which is P1884.5.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How did you find this document?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: This document -- this was I think one of the last ones I think I saw, in fact. There were a few extra buildings on it that I didn't have a chance to see. But nonetheless, this is a document which is established not in 1997, but later on. This document, if you compare it to as a narrative established by -- I think maybe it's even the same person who actually signed the cover letter to it, you discover that in the list of the fiche here, you find that you have a mosque that was destroyed in the 1940s which was said to have been destroyed during the last war. That mosque was destroyed in the 1940s, but it was put on the fiche as being destroyed in the last war. That raises some problem. That kind of information, this doesn't happen with everyone. It happens from time to time. It means that the document has to be used with a great deal of care.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dr. Kaiser, did you find this discrepancy in dates of destruction or damage only in this Kljuc document, or did you find it with other documents as well?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I believe they are established by a community on the spot. I think in Bosanski Novi, I think there are no dates, there are no specific dates for destruction. Somebody has just put 1992 on all of them, you will see. In the other documents, there is specific dates of destruction, which can be given for Kotor Varos, and you will find them, as I say, most of them in July. And I think in Donji Vakuf, there's not very much, not Kljuc, not so much in terms of dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How did you use this Kljuc document?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: This one, I don't recall using very much at all for the dates because there's nothing there. However there was a document that was established, which is a narrative of the Islamic community in the municipality of Kljuc which gave some dates. So that was of some utility. This document here on Kljuc was not so useful for dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could the interpreters explain to me the meaning of the word porusena? The interpreters in B/C/S, they could translate to me the word porusena?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it means "destroyed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see, okay. And what is the meaning of minirana?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it means "mined."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And trajno ostecena.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Trajno Ostecena.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is "permanently destroyed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we are receiving interpretation in B/C/S. On channel 4, we are receiving interpretation in B/C/S now. So it's switched on. I appreciate your interest in having us learn the language. Yes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So I will ask again the question. Bosanski Novi documents, how did you find these documents? And I'm referring to Exhibit P1884.6. Did you use this document during your work on the report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Frankly, I know this document. I checked it against a list, I think, in Muharem Omerdic. I didn't use this document very much. It's not very good.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said you checked the list of objects with Muharem Omerdic's book. Did you find in this respect the document reliable or unreliable?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: They're sort of about the same. The useful supplementary information to Omerdic's book would come from these rather odd narratives or documents which were provided independently by an imam for example in Prijedor who would list all sorts of things that existed in the municipality, or by the head of the Islamic board in Kljuc, a narrative. utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And the last one is Donji Vakuf, P1884.7.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Again, I didn't use this very much. I mean, this is the kind of document that has, for example, on the town mosque in Donji Vakuf says it was built in 1572. Okay, that's true, but it was rebuilt twice, and the minaret is left from the 16th century. Often these documents aren't very accurate even in terms of the dating of the buildings. So I didn't use this document very much. I notice this version has a few photographs in it I haven't seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One question before you proceed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, I'm sorry about that. Are you in a position to confirm to us whether these documents were compiled only, solely, for the purposes of these proceedings, for the -- for this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm a historian by training, and so I have -- we have to be sceptical of information, and we are often having to look for things internally inside of documents when we can't check them outside. I think I'm usually more rigorous than a lot of people. And a document that I -- I mentioned the documents in Prijedor, and one set of documents from the Sanski Most, religious authorities of the Islamic community, I used these because I believed they were not produced for the Tribunal. They are produced for the internal usage of the Islamic community, and they were especially looking for funds. Now, these other documents that have been -- came up later on that all have the same sort of Islamic -- the format, and by the way, these other Prijedor and Sanski Most, they had their own individual formats, okay, they were just done up in the corner, you know. These other ones are all sort of similar formats. I saw them later. I'm not sure how these have been transmitted, these documents. In Bosanski Novi, everything was destroyed in 1992. That sort of makes me nervous about what the purpose of the document is. These are documents that could have been produced for the Tribunal and for this case. It's possible. That's why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of any international fund for compensation, restructuring? I don't know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Restructuring the Islamic community? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rebuilding, sort of a compensation, international compensation, money available for the rebuilding, reconstruction of these mosques?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Sanski Most, which is now a Federation municipality, we have to go and ferret out the old pictures, because a great many of mosques have been rebuilt and new mosques have been built where there were no mosques. So, the Islamic community in Sanski Most after the war were very, very interested in securing funding for rebuilding, and these documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether -- because I'm thinking of insurance claims. Sometimes the description of the damage is inflated unlawfully. Anyway, is there anything else you would like to know about these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just about a remark about your last remark, Your Honour, is that one has to be very careful when one sees the words "completely destroyed" and "destroyed." And those words appear all the time. I'm not saying those words are written down because somebody is making up a story. Those words really very, very often correspond to a psychological reaction to something being damaged. But they appear so often, and I suppose my skepticism is pretty strong about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the course of your investigations and in the compilation of your report, you tried your level best to be as objective as possible and to present us with a picture that is in no way biased?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is exactly what I've tried to do. I think only the truth is going to help anybody in that country. And only the truth will diffuse a lot of the problems. I'm a historian, and I'm a UNESCO functionary as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham, Madam Baruch and Madam Richterova will give you an indication of how much importance the Tribunal will attach to these attachments as compared to the testimony that Dr. Kaiser will be giving and his reports. In other words, we can proceed along those lines, and that's what we precisely intend to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After the adjournment, I would like to focus primarily on the assessment of the damage to the mosques and Catholic churches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have only one more question before the break. And it is: You referred to some books. Can you tell us which books you used during your work, during your preparation for your report? You mentioned Muharem Omerdic. Did you use this book?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Yes, I used this book essentially for looking different types of buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you have the title of the book?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: "Prilozi izucanvanju genocida na Bosnjacima," I can't do the date in the local language. Published in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did you use some books by Kemal Zukic?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Yes, I've used Mr. Zukic's book, "Islamic architecture in the Balkans and Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How did you work with these books? Did you use the pictures? Did you use the information? Did you compare the information with your own findings?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Okay, with these two books, Mr. Omerdic's book is useful for trying to find something. It's not so useful for actual information on it. Mr. Zukic's books as far as six municipalities are concerned is useful mainly for the Federation municipalities to which he had access at the end of the war because there are photographs of buildings that since have simply been pulled down or rebuilt. And it is mainly from the standpoint of the photographic material in Mr. Zukic's book. This is the reason I used it. He actually doesn't indicate very much in terms of the dates of damaging which is of course important to this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dr. Kaiser, what kind of material did you use for evaluation of destruction or damage of Catholic churches?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, the Catholic church published "Raspeta Crkva" for Bosnia-Herzegovina which could be translated as crucified churches. It was published in 1997. It contains a great deal of photographic material. It also contains great many details on damaging, dates of damaging. Now, what's very important about the book is it's 1997. It wasn't produced last year, in the last six months. I think that if you look at a picture in a book sometimes and then you read the text, you'll see, well, the text is maybe not exact, doesn't give you exactly what had happened to the building in the picture. But the picture is there as well, and that's very, very important. The dating of incidents, of damaging, I think -- I really think is credible. However, this book does not indicate who is the source of information for the damaging. So we don't -- we don't know. But we do have an attempt to establish a chronology, a picture of damaging of the Roman Catholic community's buildings. Goes beyond buildings; it also includes graveyards, it includes chapels and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest we do, Madam Richterova, during the break, if you would be kind enough, Dr. Kaiser, to write down on a sheet of paper the books that you have referred to, the main ones in particular, so that we will check whether they are available in our library.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, Muharem Omerdic's book, and Kemal Zukic's book is on the CD which we provided you in the Defence, so they are in electronic form. The book "Crucified Churches," it is in the possession of the OTP, one copy. What we did for disclosure purposes, we have extracts from that book which was disclosed to the Defence. Unfortunately, we have only one spare copy. For inspection, we can, of course, provide the whole book, so the Defence, the Judges, can inspect the "Crucified Churches" book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's important. And for the time being, if you could perhaps let us have a photocopy of that extract so we will have it, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If Your Honours don't mind to have just one copy, I can provide this one copy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't need it now. We have enough to read. So take your time, and let us have a spare copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can provide you with spare copies. It won't be unfortunately today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No problem, Madam Richterova. Three copies, one for each of the three of us. So we will have a break now resuming at 11.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. [Trial Chamber and legal assistant confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, Mr. Cunningham, Ms. Korner would like five minutes to address us on the matter you brought up this morning, well, Madam Baruch, and that will be at 12.25, in other words, we'll stop with the witness at 12.25 instead of 12.30, and then we can hear what Ms. Korner has to say, and you can refer it to Mr. Ackerman. It's about tomorrow's witness in other words.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Yes, I know. And she did speak with me, just so the Court will know, and I have spoken with Mr. Ackerman about it already. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Does she still need to come?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Well, we have widely divergent views about the state of affairs, so I wouldn't want to take aware her opportunity to speak to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. So, yes, Madam Richterova, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After the break, I would like to focus on the evaluation damage, which to the sacral building, but first I want to start with one thing. You were tasked to focus on the six municipalities within the Autonomous Region of Krajina. There is a list of villages building in the indictment. Did you evaluate only those buildings which are in the indictment, or were you able to identify more buildings than stated in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, it may sound odd, but I ignored the indictment and the list of buildings that was in the indictment for those municipalities. What I attempted to do was to find all the buildings, the sacral buildings, in the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And we already heard that you used these sources, like books, Islamic community documents, and other materials to identify these buildings. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now let's focus on the damage. Just generally, which way did you use to determine the nature and the source of damage? And I forgot to mention at the beginning, if you could slow down for the interpretation so they can manage to interpret everything what is said. So first question is how to determine the nature of the damage?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, you notice from the report that I have used slightly different categories that you usually encounter, talking about damaging. First category is destroyed. For me, destroyed is usually fairly obvious. And I use destroyed to mean "destroyed." I don't mean it to have two holes in it, to have the roof off it. It means that a building has disappeared from the site, or what it could also mean, that is the building structure, the supporting walls, have been so badly damaged that the building will probably be pulled down. Now, that's not so unusual. You will find that sort of description "destroyed." But I also -- but then I talk about something repairable, and what I really sort of mean is that doesn't matter how badly damaged, it's heavily damaged, it's moderately damaged, but it can be repaired, but what I mean by repairable buildings is also usable buildings, are these buildings usable? Whatever the level of damage could be ascribed to them. So there is then a third category, and I put minor damage, which is like broken glass, pillaging, vandalism, minor damage or no damage, and I actually put them together in one category. I want to remind the Tribunal here that we are talking about events that often happened 11 years ago, and for a lot of us, although it seems like it happened yesterday, it did happen 11 years ago. And over time, over rebuilding, over -- things simply get -- they change, they change a lot. Buildings that are lightly damaged, for example, 1992, if they are still standing 11 years later, can often look rather different. How they look now doesn't really -- may not at all correspond to their situation in 1992 when they were damaged. I try to find simple and meaningful categories, and not get involved in questions of -- or arguments between experts. I worked on the cultural heritage afterwar reconstruction, so I know a lot about experts. I've seen buildings get repaired that everybody was going around saying they had been completely destroyed. It's not true. They, in fact, were repairable. The office of UNESCO worked on 45 schools for rehabilitation, and in a couple of cases, actually building the schools and equipping. So...

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Before we go to -- we will move to the pictures, I want to ask you about the method which you use to evaluate the level of damage.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, I thought that I explained the degree, the way I was proceeding. I think I made it clear for destroyed -- I'll go back to repairable. What we're talking about here -- and unusable. Remember I used these words together. Because mostly talking about the impact on a community. If we're talking about repairable, we could be talking about buildings that are heavily damaged, but I don't say they are heavily damaged. Heavily damage would mean bad damage to walls, one or two walls are missing, the roof is missing, because you will get heavy damage after the roof is gone. I would call that to be heavy damaging, the minaret -- if the minaret is down on the building, it's heavy damage. If it's down beside the building, you may not call that heavy damage. I think we're very, very often, in fact, with something we would call heavy damage in the six municipalities. But I prefer to talk about the usability and the repairability of a building first.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dr. Kaiser, when I ask you about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Madam Richterova, according to the criteria that you used in your evaluations, what would amount to a writeoff according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Writeoffs, first category, I explained. Writeoff, it disappeared. Or the structural damage to load-bearing walls is so bad that the whole thing goes. That would be total destruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will demonstrate on the pictures exactly the separate categories of damage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly, that's what we need to see here. And having finished with that, I don't think we would need to see more pictures. All I want to know is an example of a mosque that is structural beyond repair, it's a writeoff; those which have been totally demolished or destroyed, I suppose, we need to see one picture only of rubble if it's still there. And then we need to see pictures of other categories of damaged mosques. But just a sample of each, and we'll leave it at that, because otherwise we'll never finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Exactly. I just wanted -- and my question was only whether you saw these buildings by yourself, or whether you did your evaluation just based on photo materials or some other information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's my last question before we move to the pictures.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: I visited 91 per cent of the sites of mosques, mesdzids, and mektebs. Ninety-one per cent of the sites. Keep in mind a lot of things had been rebuilt. So for example in Prijedor, I had to go on photographs, and I visited 57 per cent of the sites of the Roman Catholic churches. That's a bit of a different thing. Nothing has been completely rebuilt. Things have been restored, but basic structures are there that were damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dr. Kaiser, now, can we show the examples, totally destroyed, heavily destroyed, and buildings that just sustained some minor damage. So if you could tell us which photographs you would like to show us, and I will use the hard copies which I have here. So if you could tell us which pictures you would put into category of destroyed.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Do I need numbers and things of pictures or just the names?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Just the names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just the names. And usually on top, there is a reference number, so if you could refer us to that, it can be located very easily by Ms. Gustin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First is the mosque Kevljani in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The mosque in Kevljani, it is in Prijedor. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This picture was taken by the investigators of the OTP, and it is the reason why on the top is our reference number which will be, of course, different than those which is on the CD. So please ignore this number because it is there just because it was scanned with this number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, on the CD, this would be which one? That's what we are interested in. I mean, we are not interested in the number as we see it on the monitor here if that is not the number that we should take into account. What is it on the CD?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you would be patient with me, I will provide you with ERN numbers which are on the CDs at a later stage because my hard copy is identical, but without ERN numbers. These ERN numbers are on the CD. But this document can be always very easily identified because it goes the name, which is on one page, and the following page has the image of the mosque or the church. And as I already stated, we have these tables. If Your Honour find the table for Prijedor and look up Kevljani. Do you have it, Your Honour? It is Prijedor 1, municipality Kevljani, and it is third on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't found it, but...

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And you have copies, Your Honour, with ERN numbers, so to help you, it is 03235222.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So on this occasion, you can also explain to us how this table can help us to understand your report.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: The first thing is the table is not a collection -- it's not a database. It's not a collection of fiche. What the tables are were an aid to me, and the order on the tables usually corresponds to my only visiting of them. And I used that ordering simply because I remember better from place to place. It's not conceived for you; it is conceived for me. It contains information on it which is useful to me, but also contains things like question marks because I'm asking myself questions. Sorry, I'll slow down. I ask myself questions about the buildings. It does not contain, for example, references to witness -- the witnesses. I'm not particularly interested in the witnesses when I do my table. I'm interested in the building and in the other sources. It contains some information which I'm not a hundred per cent sure of. These are my notes. What is of interest to the Tribunal is probably simply the letters in the very left-hand column, RMDD, et cetera, on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Dr. Kaiser, would you be so kind and tell us what these letters mean, RM --

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: D is destroyed. R is repairable. M is minor. Question mark is, well, do we really have a building that existed? What about this building? Because sometimes there is a question about whether something actually existed. I don't pretend to have the answers to all of them. I may be, in fact, a little bit too severe on some of these.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And we can see columns for damage and cause of damage. So can you --

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: If you see an X in the column, you realise that I have some degree of certainty that it's in the column of minor or repairable or destroyed, and there's columns also for possible types of damaging. That becomes harder to figure out over time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So let's be specific. Kevljani, what can we read from this table?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: From the table, okay. Well, I mean, do you want me to just say what's written on the table? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, please. It will help --

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: I call it a mosque because it has a minaret. It's not a mesdzid. A mesdzid doesn't have a minaret. Dating is very interesting to me. This was one of numerous mosques that was finished or was being constructed - this one is in fact finished - before the war. I'm interested in knowing that, when the mosque, in fact, or the structure I'm looking at, either the real structure on the ground or the structure that was destroyed, I'm interested in knowing when it was built, because I think it's also indicative of what some of the conditions are of the destruction of it. So prewar, 1990-1991. Historic interests, well, it's too new to be interesting. Structure, collapsed. What I mean by that is that two things we can look at in the picture if you want to look at it. One of them is the minaret is gone. The other thing is that the whole mosque structure is gone with it. This has been destroyed by mining. The minaret has been blown up with explosives, and the building behind it is also -- the building it was attached to was blown up with explosives. This is a complete writeoff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So this is an example of a completely destroyed building.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Just one other remark is this is a new building in a rural context. This is a rural mosque that is destroyed completely. And that's -- maybe that's a point we'll come back to later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you show us one more example of completely destroyed either mosque or church.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to show you the mosque in Donji Kamengrad in Sanski Most municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The ERN number on the list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So is it correct, do we read correctly from your table that this -- the damage is destroyed? That is to say, there is no damage; the building was destroyed, and it was -- the cause of this destruction was mining. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct. I've chosen this because this part of the structure which is part of the building structure is still standing, but this would have to be pulled down. It's so badly damaged. It was pulled down, and there is a new mosque on this site. Just one other possible remark --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But, Ms. Richterova, you mentioned Donji Kamengrad. On 5232, I can't see --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is right on the bottom, and it goes to the following page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are different. They are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Donji Kamengrad on the one -- on the one page Donji and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They are not the same. They are not the same. The one on page 5232, at the bottom, is not the one -- no, it's Kamengrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's on table 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. All right. Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are a number of buildings in this area called Donji Kamengrad. This is -- as I said, this is something left. You can pull it down. It was pulled down. The other thing is that this is very expert kind of mining, and I'll come back to this maybe later on because in fact the building has been destroyed by mining in the rear, in such a way to bring down the building structure. But not in all four corners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One question: When under the column "date of damage" when we see 27/7/92, and then SMIC.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sanski Most Islamic community. This is the 1997 record -- that's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to make that clear. And also, I notice on some of the documents, there is a description, instead of "mosque" it's called mekteb. What's a mekteb.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mekteb is a small Koranic school. Often it's a house, looks like a house. Hasn't got any minaret. It has a mehrab [phoen]. It can be used as a place for prayer as well. Usually is, in small communities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dr. Kaiser, you just mentioned that in your opinion, this was done in a professional way. Were you able to obvious when a mosque or any sacral building was destroyed or damaged professionally, as you say, and when the damage or destruction was done unprofessionally? How would you -- how would you judge this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, if we get around to more pictures later on, you'll be able to see a few examples of buildings that have not been professionally damaged or approached. For example, you'll see variants on the mining of the rear of a mosque, and somebody had an idea and somebody told them that was the way to do it but it didn't work. There's a problem because the damaging of mosques, buildings, doesn't necessarily take place at the same time, it takes place over time. It's very hard to sometimes correlate photographs, correlate testimony, correlate dates. But there are a few examples. I haven't put them in this particular case. But in Sanski Most, you'll see other examples of nonprofessional mining and examples also of professional destruction. The witnesses' testimony often indicates whether it's done professionally or not. In Sanski Most, the town, the main town mosque seems to have been mined about three times. And one of the pictures taken after the second mining, and it shows this not being done in the proper -- excuse me, using the expression not the proper way, but it's not being done in a particularly professional way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. We will go through this in details when we go through Sanski Most. So we have two examples of totally destroyed buildings which you put into category "unrepairable." Now, can you tell us some examples of repairable building which you said was heavily damaged but still in your opinion repairable.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: You're going to have to get out your tables again, and we go to a mosque in Gornji Jakupovici, also in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is also on the 03235223.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So if you could make comment on this picture.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, I think this is going to explain why I talk about things that are repairable. This is -- this mosque, as you can see, was damaged clearly by mining on the minaret, which is where -- you see the ladder, there on the left. There's another picture which comes from the earlier collection done by the Islamic community in Prijedor, which actually shows the minaret leaning over on the roof. Now, some people would say it was destroyed. Well, fortunately, these optimistic people said "no, it's not destroyed." The evaluation by this engineer who was working for the Islamic community said "it's not destroyed." This is being repaired. That is what was damaged was of course the walls of the corner, the roof, and people are putting it back together. That's a repairable mosque. But it's badly damaged. Now, I noted, and I can't remember exactly perhaps why, that the roof was gone. And I thought it was a question of firing. Sometimes it's firing; sometimes the roof is removed. Maybe the firing is -- it's also evident, attempt to fire from the picture that was taken from the Islamic community.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we see one more example of repairable building.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: One?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: One more example.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Okay, let's go to, in that case, to Bosanski Novi, and Donji Agici, the mosque in Celopek.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is on the page 03235208.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If you could make a comment on this picture. Is it correct that it is one of your pictures?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, this is one of mine, my pictures. One thing I should say is that I didn't systematically take pictures because if there were good pictures from the ICTY investigators, I used them. They took very bad pictures of this, so this is why I took it. This changes from other buildings that we've seen. This is a stone mosque. I'm not sure when it was built. Maybe it was built in the 1930s. It's a stone mosque. It had a country mosque. It had the minaret in the roof. Now, there would happen to be a local standing there and explained to me how it happened. They blew up the minaret in the roof. The roof structure collapsed. So the building was unusable. Didn't burn, and if anybody wants to put the roof back, it's okay, could be used. It should be noticed that the third building down the road, that's the new mosque. And the new mosque was unfinished before the war. And the door was mined after the war, according to a local person. It wasn't touched during the war. So that's the kind of situation. If you want to have the old mosque, nice old stone mosque, it's still there to be used. But the intention was clearly to build a new mosque a little bit down the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other one is a memento mori.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope not. It's a nicer building, the stone one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we have now an example of a building which you evaluate as -- it sustained just a minor damage.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we have just one example.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, I said, minor or no damage. And so one that has a little bit of damage may be -- let's go to Demisevci mekteb in Sanski Most. It's number 5, table 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is the very last page, it is 02325237.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can see in your table that you call this structure mekteb. We already mentioned that a mekteb was used for praying, but the primary purpose was or is it's a school to teach Koran. Mekteb, does it have a minaret?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Mekteb doesn't have a minaret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has already explained that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So do you have an explanation why the buildings with minarets were damaged? And this, as we can see, didn't taken almost any damage?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, the discussion about the minaret is a big discussion in its own right. I mean, if you want me to enter into that discussion, okay, I will. But if we want to talk about first this, then --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Let's first talk about this, and then I would like to hear your conclusion on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, Madam Richterova, sorry to butt in again, but I need to know whether the mosque or the construction we are seeing in this photo is the newly constructed building or whether it's the old mekteb that was damaged and, according to what I have here, pulled down. So what am I looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What you're looking at is a building I didn't see. This is a photograph that was taken in early -- well, maybe the fall of 1996. Systematic collection of photographs taken of the Islamic community properties. This was in Demisevci. I went to look for this in Demisevci, and we couldn't find it in Demisevci, but we could find a new mosque going up on the location. This had been pulled down just very, very recently. We're looking at the mekteb that was built probably after World War II. It looks like a house. I say it's pillaged because there are other photos that showed a little bit of trashing inside. You can see a window broken on the outside. This is a building that missed destruction in Sanski Most Municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If we could go back, do you have any theory why these mekteb and mesdzid survived generally and why the mosque with minaret were usually attacked?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: I think you've heard this before that there is a link --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, Dr. Kaiser, would you agree with this statement to start with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if you have an explanation, perhaps you could answer the question. But first of all I needed to know if you agree with what has been put to you as a statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, if your target is the mosque and the minaret, and especially the minaret, it's an easy thing to find. It's quite clear that minarets are targeted specifically. You will find lots of examples of a minaret has gone down first. Sometimes somebody will come back and get the rest of the building; sometimes not. In the very first picture that we saw of Kevljani, we saw a minaret on the ground, and we also saw the building in the background. It's highly possible in Kevljani somebody came and first destroyed the minaret, and then came back and destroyed the rest of the building. Buildings will be standing. The minarets will be gone. I can give you -- show you an example of unfinished building which were usually not much attention was given to them in Vrhpolje. There's an unfinished mosque, but it had a minaret. They went and got the minaret. But they didn't touch the rest of the building. The minaret was singled out for destruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you agree that the minaret is the distinctive feature of a mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The minaret is the sign, either in a town or especially in the countryside that there is a Muslim community because the minaret, especially the minarets of the new mosques. You saw a little while ago a mosque which I said its minaret was in the roof. You can't see those. But in the 1970s, the 1980s, there began to be minarets all over the countryside. And the minaret of where the Muslim lives. If you eliminate the Muslim from the countryside, physically the person, you can also eliminate the idea, the sign, the memory, you eliminate first of all the minaret. And then maybe you get around to the rest of the building. I think there was only one minaret that was found still standing in Republika Srpska after the war. I've seen one in Kupres that was an unfinished minaret. It was not knocked down. That means if you don't have a minaret on the building, already the interest in that building is somewhat less. A lot of mesdzids are, in fact, burned. A lot of mektebs, though, they look houses, so they're not destroyed. Maybe that raises another question, who is doing the destroying? If it's local guys, they know where all these places are. The mektebs and the mesdzids and the ones that look like houses. That's a question that has come to mind especially to me working on this case. Does that answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: That answers the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In your report, you prepared a table in which you stated how many -- it is on page 4 of your report. And in your -- in this table, you have destroyed sacral buildings, repairable, and minor or no damage. And you broke down the table according to municipalities.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can see the total number of destroyed is 37; repairable, 61; minor or no damage, 14. And then you have numbers or figures for buildings which you were not able to evaluate. Is it correct what is stated in your report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Yes, the bottom figures are correct in that table.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you want to add something to your findings which are in your report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Well, the numbers are there, but I think it's the percentages which I think are of particular interest. We're talking about the Islamic sacral buildings, and I mean, 29 -- saying what I could prove, what I was satisfied with, prove that 29 per cent of the Islamic buildings were destroyed. Three in ten are definitely destroyed; 48 per cent are badly damaged; 77 per cent demonstrably unusable. If you start looking at these other categories, something has been replaced, something you couldn't find it, there wasn't any information, maybe ten months later you discovered the fact that it was there, you start getting up to certainly between 80 and 85 per cent of the Islamic sacral buildings unusable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will be able to refer specifically to where we need to look at. This table that you have just been referred to, I take it it covers the period 1992-1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the purposes of this trial, we are now interested in the mosques and other religious buildings that were possibly damaged or destroyed either before or after the period covered by the indictment, which is part of 1992 and part of 1993. So where do we need to go to establish which religious buildings were destroyed during this period only, and not at some other -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I may be confused, but was it not 1991 and 1992 for this particular indictment? No, it was 1992 and 1993. 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1992 and also I think part of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, just until 31st of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1992. But that's what we are interested in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In your report, on page 7, you provided some kind of chronology of damage and destruction of Islamic sacral buildings and Catholic churches, and you focus on the year 1992. Can you now elaborate on this part of your report.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Okay, yes. Page 7 of the report you have information -- okay, for all the years, because that has to be sorted out first. That comes from the secondary sources only. Only secondary sources. So you can see that according to the secondary sources, the far greatest number of damaging or destruction occurs in 1992. Sometimes those sources say 1992; they don't say 1st of August, 1992. So you have to go, when talking about the secondary sources, you have to go now to the next step, and the next step is to say, well, do they something about the months of damaging? Page 8, we go on with this kind of further refinement for municipalities. Now this table shows a smaller number than the number that's in the first table, 1992, because now we have some sort of date indicated, some sort of month. We also, for example, for Sanski Most, we have a mining given the date of April from a secondary source. That's very early. I hope I'm not going too quickly for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have problems, interpreters, please give me a sign, okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you're doing fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. The second table, then, shows, if you take a look at it, it looks -- it seems that -- excuse me. The second table shows that according to secondary sources, giving months of damaging, May, June, July, and August, in these four municipalities seem to be months of a lot of activity towards mosques. That's secondary sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Excuse me. When we are talking about secondary sources, can you again probably repeat what kind of sources you were using?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER
utterances.text: Okay, these are the sources from the Islamic community that I'm particularly -- I have some confidence in. Sometimes it's -- I put them there because I'm not quite sure, but they're interesting. They deserve to be sort of cross-referenced with what the witnesses will say. We're talking only about the Islamic community now, but it's mainly Islamic community sources here in this particular table. Then we go on to something which is different; that is, witnesses.
